kind: coordinator synthesis, CORRECTED against Squad B's row-2 defence
supersedes: the first version of pack-append-synthesis.json, whose object_packs_data_bytes, measured/derived status and uniform-amplification model were all wrong
corrections: object_packs data is 302,023,232 bytes, not 304,427,008. The larger figure came from SQLite dbstat, which reports PAGE bytes (304,427,008) and not payload bytes. The receipt publishes resources.space.pack_bodies_bytes = 302023232, which equals SELECT SUM(length(data)) FROM object_packs exactly.

The amplification is MEASURED, not derived. The claim in the first version that 'the store keeps only final pack lengths, so the intermediate lengths cannot be read back' is FALSE: the pack directory stores body_start/encoded/decoded per group (core/crates/layerfs-storage/src/pack/layout.rs:331-393) plus a 4-byte start offset for the compact whole-file lane (:397-454). Squad B read all 1,250 directories and reproduced every intermediate length, asserting Sigma(entry+body) == length(data) per pack with 0 failures.
The average pack rewrite is ~134 KiB (median 137,544 B), not 243 KB. 243 KB sits between p90 and the max, near PACK_LIMIT = 262,144.
Amplification is NOT uniform across lanes, so a single global (k+1)/2 factor is the wrong shape.

The candidate in the first version's section 13.5 - 'hold the tail and issue one UPDATE per pack per transaction' - is ALREADY THE BEHAVIOUR and can reduce nothing: appends are already one per affected pack per transaction, and no code path writes the same pack twice inside one transaction (cas/placement.rs:161 takes writes.first() and there is exactly one write to take).

measured_amplification.method: sum of every pack directory's intermediate data lengths across all 16,802 writes, read out of the 1,250 pack directories

skew: WholeFile + PooledMetadata rewrite 56.1% of all rewritten bytes to persist 8.4% of the final bytes. WholeFile is extreme because cas/selection.rs:57-58 and :97-102 seals that lane after every single member, so 9,444 one-record seals land in 102 packs and ~2.6 KB of new data drags a ~241 KB body through SQLite again.

what_it_established: The same pack-append amplification on a different lane: 'every pack append rewrites a whole pack body (255 packs, 45,298,203 bytes, 177,640 average, 262,112 maximum -> about 8.1 GB of BLOB rewritten across 45,794 appends)'.
A COMMIT cost of 58.0 us with journal_mode=MEMORY and synchronous=OFF - 96% of that lane's commit_ns bucket - for the same reason.

That the commit cadence is a CONTRACT: widening the step via a LAYERFS_STORAGE_COMMIT_EVERY knob made the second writer FAIL with CleanupFailed { original: OwnershipUnavailable, .. } at every value above 1.
prior_art.what_is_new_here: The amplification is reproduced at 10,000-file scale with a per-lane breakdown (3.64x to 51.21x) that localises it to two lanes, and the WholeFile seal rule that causes it is identified at cas/selection.rs:57-58, :97-102. The phenomenon itself is NOT new to this campaign and must not be presented as a discovery.
prior_art.knob_status: LAYERFS_STORAGE_COMMIT_EVERY does not exist anywhere in core/ or crates/ at HEAD 9c46930b8; the contract is now structural rather than a knob.
